Question Choices: Select all the letters that have a vertical line of symmetry. A letter may also have a horizontal line of symmetry. Use ideal upright capital letters with uniform strokes and no serifs: A has equal sloping sides and a centred crossbar; H has equal vertical posts joined at their midpoints; T has a centred post below its top bar; P has a left post and an upper loop only on its right. ~~A | H | P | T~~
Hints: A vertical reflection exchanges the left and right halves. Another valid reflection line does not disqualify a letter.
Solution: A has matching sloping sides, H has matching posts, and T has a centred post and matching halves of its top bar. Each has a vertical line of symmetry. P does not: its right loop has no matching left loop. Select A, H and T. H also has a horizontal line of symmetry.

Question Choices: Select. A shape has no lines of symmetry. Which of these could it be?: ~~A | B | C | D~~
Hints: A symmetry line must reflect the entire shape exactly onto itself.
Solution: A is scalene: its three sides differ, so no reflection exchanges matching sides. B (square)has 4 lines,C(isosceles triangle)has 1 vertical line,D(circle)has infinitely many.

Question Choices: Select. A shape has exactly four lines of symmetry.: ~~A | B | C | D~~
Hints: Test vertical, horizontal and diagonal folds. A non-square rectangle has two; a square has four.
Solution: The square B has exactly 4 axes:vertical,horizontal andboth diagonals. A has 0,C 1,D infinitely many.

Question Choices: Fill: This shape has exactly 6 lines of symmetry. It is a polygon, and all its sides and angles are equal. This shape must be a ________. (triangle or square or pentagon or hexagon)
Hints: A regular polygon has the same number of symmetry lines as sides.
Solution: A regular polygon has as many symmetry lines as sides. Six axes therefore identify a regular hexagon.

Question Choices: True or False: Every line that passes through the center of a square is a line of symmetry.
Hints: Test vertical, horizontal and diagonal folds. A non-square rectangle has two; a square has four.
Solution: A square has only four symmetry lines:two diagonals and two lines through opposite side midpoints. Most other lines through its centre fail to match the sides and vertices.
